s1.syndrome_frame: A clinical presentation of acute abdominal and respiratory symptoms with altered mental status in a patient with chronic kidney disease and immunosuppression
salient_findings: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and altered mental status
Colonic wall thickening and cavitary lung lesion on imaging
Presence of Strongyloides filaria and Aspergillus on bronchoscopy and bronchoalveolar lavage
key_facts: Patient is a 43-year-old woman with stage IV chronic kidney disease
Patient is being treated with cyclophosphamide, prednisone, and hydroxychloroquine
Patient has not left the United States for 14 years
Heart rate is 110 beats per minute
Stool ova and parasite test is positive
CT abdomen shows colonic wall thickening
CT chest shows a cavitary lung lesion in the right base and diffuse tree-in-bud pattern infiltrates
Bronchoalveolar lavage is positive for Aspergillus

shortlist.label: Strongyloidiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a positive stool ova and parasite test and bronchoscopy revealed Strongyloides filaria

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a positive bronchoalveolar lavage for Aspergillus and a high serum 1-3-β-D-glucan level

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunosuppressed and has respiratory symptoms with diffuse tree-in-bud pattern infiltrates on CT chest

shortlist.label: Sepsis syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a high temperature, heart rate, and blood pressure, and is showing signs of organ dysfunction

shortlist.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a cavitary lung lesion and altered mental status, which could be indicative of disseminated TB

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including the presence of Strongyloides filaria in the bronchoscopy and positive stool ova and parasite test, strongly support this diagnosis. The patient's immunosuppressed state due to treatment with cyclophosphamide and prednisone also increases the risk of strongyloidiasis.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a positive bronchoalveolar lavage for Aspergillus, the presence of Strongyloides filaria and positive stool ova and parasite test are more specific for strongyloidiasis.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the case facts to support this diagnosis, such as a positive PCR test for Pneumocystis jirovecii.

rejected.label: Sepsis syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a fever and abnormal vital signs, the presence of specific pathogens such as Strongyloides filaria and Aspergillus suggest a more specific diagnosis than sepsis syndrome.

rejected.label: Disseminated tuberculosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the case facts to support this diagnosis, such as a positive culture or PCR test for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

gold: Disseminated Strongyloides infection with concurrent Aspergillus infection
